newsitem.title: USA: Piper recovered in May, June after slow Q3 start.
newsitem.headline: Piper recovered in May, June after slow Q3 start.

text.p: Piper Jaffray Cos Inc, an investment firm, said it experienced a recovery in May and June after a slow start to its fiscal third quarter, which ended June 30.
"Our third quarter got off to a slow start, but I'm encouraged by the strong recovery we made in May and June," Addison Piper, chairman, said in a statement.
Piper Jaffray today reported earnings for the third quarter of $0.34 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.08 after a $15.5 million charge to settle a class action lawsuit.
Revenue for the quarter was $145.4 million, down from $147.6 million a year ago. In the first nine months of the year, revenues were $437.5 million, up five percent from a year ago.
Piper said its fiscal third quarter was weak for many in the securities industry due to lower equity trading volumes and a slowdown in underwriting activty.
Individual investor services revenue continued to grow, with particularly strong contributions from offices in the Washignton, California and Arizona/Utah regions.

Fixed-income capital markets revenue was also strong for the first nine months. School financing issues in California, Nevada and Iowa totaling more than $1.4 billion, and several large taxable syndicate deals, contributed to the increase.

During the first nine months of the year, fixed-income capital markets managed or co-managed 590 tax-exempt issues worth $9.6 billion. That compared to 469 tax-exempt issues with a volume of $8.0 billion in the year-ago period.
Equity capital markets revenues for the first nine months were below a year ago.

As previously reported, Piper continues to be a defendant in lawsuits or arbitrations related to various funds or assets managed by Piper Capital. It is cooperating in investigations being conducted by the Securities and Exchange Commission and other regulatory agencies.

No provision for a loss that could result has been recorded, and the aggregate cost of litigation and any judgments could have a material, adverse effect. Piper reiterated it believes the litigation exposure is manageable.
